LESSON: BAR GRAPHS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: DATA HANDLING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Ex
Topic 4.1: Bar Graphs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Bar Graphs, part of DATA HANDLING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Ex in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you represent data in real life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Bar Graphs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: The learner makes connections when collecting data and organizing them in pictographs,

frequency tables, bar graphs or by piling.

● Digital literacy: The learner develops interactive and connecting skills when using digital devices with assistive technology

to learn more on data representation using bar graphs.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes care of the various learning resources used in collecting, recording and representing

data.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety and security: The learner takes care of themselves and others when collecting data from the environment.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Creative arts: The learner collects data from the environment and represents it in pictographs or bar graphs.

Suggested Learning Resources

Sticks, glue, pair of scissors, wire, soft board, reference materials in Braille and appropriate print, real objects such as

matchboxes, cubes, cuboids
